audit_findings.title: A mostly uncollected, one-time tariff recovery appears embedded in recurring owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $98.3m pre-tax and $90.0m after-tax FY2026 income; $114.7m receivable with only $2.1m collected; $90.0m equals 8.3% of the $1,089.9m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The nonrecurring income raises FY2026 OE and therefore the log-trend anchor; the associated receivable requires separate bridge treatment rather than perpetual capitalization.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company estimates the amount of the probable refund to be $114.7 million, of which $96.2 million was recognized as a reduction to Cost of sales, $9.5 million was recorded as Accrued liabilities and $9.0 million was applied as a reduction to tariffs that remained in Inventory.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated classification error, not merely a collection-risk possibility. An after-tax item equal to 8.3% of the selected anchor is large enough to affect the fair-value range when capitalized, although correcting it would reinforce rather than reverse the supplied no-buy conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Remove the filed $90.0m after-tax refund benefit from FY2026 OE, refit the log trend, and separately add only the risk-adjusted present value of the $114.7m receivable without double counting cash already collected.

audit_findings.title: The selected trend anchor omits the most recent comparative year
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2025 filed net income was $183.2m versus $1,134.2m excluding comparability items, while FY2026 net income was $1,527.7m
audit_findings.mechanism: The missing FY2025 OE observation directly affects the historical log trend that sets the $1,089.9m anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Net income increased $1.34 billion to $1.53 billion in fiscal 2026 as compared to $183.2 million in fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated, but its direction cannot be established until FY2025 OE is reconstructed. Given the $951.0m after-tax comparability adjustment in FY2025 and the anchor's dependence on the trend, a valid FY2025 observation is reasonably capable of changing the valuation result.
audit_findings.action: Resolve the FY2025 D&A classification, calculate FY2025 OE using the same one-off rules as every other year, and rerun the trend-anchor selection and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Known post-year-end tariffs are absent from the historical run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; announced rates are 10%-12.5%, while tariffs reduced FY2026 adjusted gross margin by approximately 130 basis points
audit_findings.mechanism: Post-year-end tariffs can reduce future gross margin and OE, so historical margins combined with positive growth may overstate forecast cash earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: On July 23, 2026, the U.S. Administration announced the final remedy in the Section 301 investigations relating to forced labor practices, imposing new tariff rates ranging from 10% to 12.5% on most imports from certain countries, effective upon the expiration of the temporary Section 122 tariffs.
audit_findings.explanation: The tariff rates were known at the valuation date, but the filing does not quantify applicable imports, duration, pricing offsets, sourcing mitigation or the resulting OE impact. This is a forward-looking exposure rather than a demonstrated error in historical OE.
audit_findings.action: Estimate annual tariff cost by sourcing country and U.S. import volume, net of evidenced pricing and sourcing mitigation, then verify that bear, base and bull OE forecasts absorb the resulting margin effect.

audit_findings.title: A $150 million tax claim may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $150.0m, equal to $0.72 per diluted share and 0.91% of the $16,465m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any settlement not captured in forecast cash taxes is a claim against equity and should reduce the bridge or future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Excluded from the above contractual obligations table is the non-current liability, including related interest and penalties, for unrecognized tax benefits of $150.0 million as of June 27, 2026, as we cannot make a reliable estimate of the period in which the liability will be settled, if ever.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability is filed and the bridge does not expressly address it, but even deducting the entire undiscounted $150.0m would reduce base value from $79.35 to approximately $78.63 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $122.14 price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether expected settlement is already captured in forecast cash taxes; otherwise show an expected-present-value bridge deduction, while retaining the full $150.0m deduction as an immateriality sensitivity.

audit_findings.title: Historical OE and the current business perimeter are not fully comparable
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2024 operating loss $21.2m, FY2025 adjusted operating loss $14.8m, FY2026 operating loss $1.0m, and sale proceeds $109.1m; earlier-year OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Historical OE used in the trend includes Stuart Weitzman operations and disposal effects, while the current business excludes that operation and cash includes the sale proceeds.
audit_findings.evidence: On August 4, 2025, the Company completed the sale of the Stuart Weitzman business and, as a result, determined it had two reportable segments on a prospective basis.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated and recent operating losses were small relative to the $1,089.9m anchor, but the record does not quantify Stuart Weitzman's OE contribution across the full trend period. Consequently, neither direction nor materiality of the anchor effect is established.
audit_findings.action: Restate every affected historical OE year for Stuart Weitzman operations and disposal costs, preserve the $109.1m proceeds only through the balance-sheet bridge, and rerun the log trend.

audit_findings.title: Asset-retirement cash obligations may escape both OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $65.0m, equal to $0.31 per diluted share and 0.39% of the $16,465m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Restoration cash payments could be omitted if the related depreciation is added back and neither maintenance reinvestment nor the equity bridge captures settlement of the liability.
audit_findings.evidence: As of the end of fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2025, the Company had asset retirement obligations of $65.0 million and $58.4 million, respectively, primarily classified within Other non-current liabilities in the Company's Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the obligation is already captured remains unresolved, but deducting the full undiscounted $65.0m would reduce base value from $79.35 to approximately $79.04 per share. That concrete maximum-face-value comparison cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace expected ARO settlements into maintenance reinvestment and OE; if absent, include their present value as a bridge deduction, with $65.0m as the conservative undiscounted ceiling.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: computed residuals of approximately $26.8m in FY2018, $5.9m in FY2021 and $6.6m in FY2023, totaling approximately $39.3m across three years; the largest is 2.5% of the $1,089.9m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible residual D&A, if identified, would be added back to the affected historical OE observations and could modestly raise the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2018 $233.4m (89.7% of filed D&A); FY2021 $212.8m (97.3% of filed D&A); FY2023 $175.7m (96.4% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The current treatment is demonstrably conservative and cannot overstate value. Even assuming every residual is eligible, approximately $39.3m is spread across three trend observations, and the largest single-year amount is only about 2.5% of the anchor, insufficient to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual D&A from filed notes or supporting schedules and rerun only if evidence shows eligible add-backs materially exceed these computed residual amounts.
